**April 6 Youth Movement**
An Egyptian activist group founded in 2008 to support a planned April 6 strike by textile workers in the industrial city of Mahalla al-Kubra. It modeled its nonviolent tactics and clenched-fist logo on Otpor!, the Serbian student movement that helped topple Slobodan Milošević, and it played a leading role in the 2011 revolution.

**Abdel Fattah el-Sisi**
The army chief who led the military's overthrow of President Mohamed Morsi in 2013 and became Egypt's president in 2014. His rule has been marked by harsh repression of dissent and a struggling economy.

**Mohamed Morsi and the Muslim Brotherhood**
Morsi, a leader of the Islamist Muslim Brotherhood, won the 2012 presidential runoff to become Egypt's first democratically elected president. After mass protests against his rule, the military removed him in July 2013, and he died in court in 2019 while on trial.

**Hosni Mubarak**
Egypt's president from 1981 until he was forced to resign during the 2011 revolution. In June 2012 he was sentenced to life in prison for complicity in the killing of protesters, though the conviction was later overturned.

**2012 presidential election**
Egypt's first free presidential election after Mubarak's fall. Its runoff pitted Morsi, the Muslim Brotherhood's candidate, against Ahmed Shafik, a former air force commander who had served as Mubarak's last prime minister, and Morsi narrowly won.

**Freedom and Justice Party**
The political party founded by the Muslim Brotherhood in 2011. It won the largest share of seats in the 2011–2012 parliamentary elections and was later dissolved by court order after Morsi's ouster.

**Amr Moussa**
A former Egyptian foreign minister and secretary-general of the Arab League, who was an early front-runner in the 2012 presidential race. He lost support during the campaign and failed to make the runoff.

**Tamarod**
Arabic for "rebellion," a grassroots campaign launched in 2013 that claimed to have gathered over 20 million signatures demanding Morsi's resignation. Its mass protests on June 30, 2013 preceded the military coup that removed him.

**Metrojet Flight 9268**
A Russian charter flight from the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh to St. Petersburg that broke apart over the Sinai Peninsula in October 2015, killing all 224 people on board. The Sinai branch of the Islamic State claimed responsibility for planting a bomb on the plane.

**EgyptAir hijacking and the iPhone-case bomb**
In March 2016, Seif Eldin Mustafa hijacked an EgyptAir domestic flight from Alexandria to Cairo and forced it to land in Larnaca, Cyprus. His "suicide belt" turned out to be fake, made of iPhone cases, and all passengers were released unharmed.

**Sisi's "sell myself" speech and the eBay listing**
In a 2016 speech about Egypt's economic troubles, Sisi declared that he would sell himself if it would help the country. Mocking Egyptians then listed him for sale on eBay before the listing was removed.

**Sisi's red carpet**
In 2016 Sisi was criticized for having a red carpet several kilometers long unrolled along a road for his motorcade at a time of economic austerity. His government defended it as a reusable carpet used for official ceremonies.

**Anwar al-Balkimy's nose job**
A member of parliament from the Salafist Nour Party who claimed in 2012 that he had been beaten and robbed by gunmen. It emerged that his bandaged face was actually the result of a nose job, and he resigned from the party in disgrace.

**Hazem Salah Abu Ismail**
A popular Salafist preacher disqualified from the 2012 presidential race because his mother had held United States citizenship, which Egyptian election rules prohibited for a candidate's parents.

**2011 attack on the Israeli embassy**
In September 2011, protesters in Cairo broke into the building housing Israel's embassy, forcing the evacuation of the ambassador and most staff. The attack followed anger over the killing of Egyptian border guards during an Israeli pursuit of militants.
